authors: P. Michanek; T. Toth; E. Bergstrom; H. Treffenberg-Pettersson; A. Bergh
title: Effect of infrared and red monochromatic light on equine wound healing
tissue_or_site: Experimental 2 cm wounds on both sides of the neck
dose_or_settings: 637 nm: 2.3 mW/cm2 for 95 seconds; 956 nm: 6.4 mW/cm2 for 185 seconds; once daily on days 0-4, 7-11, 14-18 and 21-25; 20 sessions
design: Randomized, blinded; one wound illuminated and the opposite wound untreated in each horse
main_result: No wound-area or swelling difference; illuminated wounds healed later: 51.8 versus 49.0 days (P=.03). No clinically relevant positive effect was demonstrated.
limits: Experimental neck skin, not hoof or fetlock disease. Treatment ended on day 25. Pulse frequency and J/cm2 were not in the abstract; no calculated dose is exported.

authors: S. P. L. Luna; A. Schoen; P. H. E. Trindade; P. B. D. Rocha
title: Penetration Profiles of a Class IV Therapeutic Laser and a Photobiomodulation Therapy Device in Equine Skin
modality: Class IV laser and portable PBMT device
dose_or_settings: Optical power measured through skin for 120 seconds; 6 light-skinned and 6 dark-skinned horses
main_result: Reported transmission was 0.01303 +/- 0.00778 for PBMT versus 0.00122 +/- 0.00070 for Class IV laser (P<.001); skin color affected transmission.
limits: Abstract did not specify transmission units, device models or wavelengths. Values must not be converted to percentages. No clinical outcome or hoof penetration measured.

title: A Systematic Literature Review of Complementary and Alternative Veterinary Medicine: Laser Therapy
tissue_or_site: Multiple sites; equine skin, tendons and joints; laminitis case series
dose_or_settings: Varied; review examples: CO2 laser 60 J/cm2; fetlock trial 91 J/cm2; tendon trial 16 J/cm2
design: Systematic review; three databases; literature from 1980-2020; meta-analysis not feasible
main_result: Most indications lacked adequate evidence of benefit; equine findings were mixed, with frequent high or moderate bias and incomplete dose reporting.
limits: 45 studies across species, not 45 horses. Laser-heavy evidence does not validate consumer LED wraps. Laminitis evidence included an uncontrolled 21-horse laser-acupuncture series. No hoof-transmission study in the read section.

title: Disorders of the Fetlock and Pastern in Horses
tissue_or_site: Fetlock and pastern; digital tendon sheath
main_result: Uncomplicated windpuffs without lameness need no treatment; swelling in only one leg can indicate a problem.
limits: Owner version; last modified September 2024. No light therapy evidence; guidance does not diagnose an individual horse.

title: First Aid for Horse Owners
tissue_or_site: Lower limbs and hoof; general equine first aid
main_result: Guidance distinguishes painful single-limb swelling from painless stocking up and describes abscess care; it does not mention light, laser or LED.
limits: First-aid guidance, not a light trial. No numeric abscess soaking duration or recovery time. Normal adult vital signs are not abscess-specific thresholds.

title: Stocking Up in Horses
main_result: Simple stocking up usually subsides after approximately 30 minutes of light exercise; heat, pain, lameness or persistent swelling warrants veterinary review.
limits: Practitioner advice from a commercial retailer; approximately 30 minutes and 12-hour bandage cycles are not trial findings. No light therapy evidence.

title: Bruised sole in horses
main_result: Rest, soft bedding and appropriate protection are described for sole bruising; uncomplicated bruises usually resolve in approximately two weeks.
limits: Guidance, not a controlled trial. Boots and pads on hard or stony ground should be used only with farrier or veterinarian direction; recovery varies. No light therapy evidence.

title: Horse hoof abscesses
main_result: Repeated daily warm-water and Epsom-salt soaking may damage the hoof; mild infections may allow return to work in less than one week.
limits: Reviewed in 2021. No numeric soaking schedule or light therapy evidence. Deep infections may take several weeks; the recovery statement is conditional.

title: Hoof Abscesses in Horses
main_result: Lameness should improve markedly within 12 hours of drainage; guidance describes medicated poultice bandaging for 3-5 days afterward.
limits: Veterinary reference, not an experimental trial. No light therapy, Epsom-salt schedule or total recovery duration stated. Excessive paring is contraindicated.

title: Subsolar Abscess and Coffin Bone Osteomyelitis
main_result: Guidance calls for prompt veterinary attention; unresolved abscesses can involve bone. Fever above 101.5 F is listed among possible signs.
limits: No publication date or light therapy evidence. Approximately 1 cm/month hoof-wall growth and postoperative bandage intervals concern surgical bone cases, not uncomplicated abscess recovery.

title: How FDA Regulates Animal Devices
main_result: Animal-only devices do not require premarket 510(k), PMA or other approval applications; FDA retains regulatory authority over such devices.
limits: Regulatory guidance, not efficacy evidence or a decision about a particular equine product. Additional radiation-product rules may apply.

title: Important Reminders about Registration and Listing
main_result: Device registration and listing do not mean FDA approval, clearance or authorization; FDA does not issue device-establishment registration certificates.
limits: Human-device registration context; animal-only obligations must be considered separately. No clinical efficacy evidence.

title: Health Products Compliance Guidance
main_result: Health claims require competent and reliable scientific support appropriate to the product and claimed outcome; testimonials do not establish causation.
limits: General advertising guidance, not an equine PBM assessment or a requirement to test equine claims in humans.

title: Businessperson's Guide to Federal Warranty Law
main_result: Written warranties are optional; if offered, applicable requirements apply. Absence of a written warranty does not eliminate all implied-warranty rights.
limits: General consumer-product guidance; state law and transaction type matter. No particular equine product warranty is established.

title: Using Credit Cards and Disputing Charges
main_result: Written billing-error disputes must reach the card issuer within 60 days after the first statement containing the error was sent.
limits: Credit-card billing guidance; accepted-goods quality disputes can have different conditions. Not a guaranteed refund or a debit-card rule.

title: Online Shopping
main_result: Guidance recommends researching sellers, keeping purchase records and evaluating reviews across sources rather than relying only on star ratings.
limits: Only the opening and review-evaluation sections were read; later sections timed out. No seller certification or clinical evidence.

title: State consumer protection offices
main_result: The directory links users to state or territorial consumer protection offices for complaints and related assistance.
limits: A directory does not guarantee a refund or identical office powers and timelines.

title: Veterinary Regulations 2026, Chapter VI
journal_or_publisher: FEI; copy hosted by British Equestrian
main_result: Article 1062 lists LED devices and Class I-III lasers as non-restricted supportive therapies; Article 1065 prohibits Class IV lasers at FEI events.
limits: Effective January 1, 2026; read cover and pages 57-58. Later amendments were not independently verified. The five-day restriction concerns cryotherapy and shockwave, not LED.

title: Mechanisms and applications of the anti-inflammatory effects of photobiomodulation
tissue_or_site: Cells and tissues; general PBM mechanisms
design: Mechanistic review; publisher abstract and mechanism sections of PDF read
main_result: The review discusses cytochrome-c-oxidase, nitric-oxide and ATP pathways and a potentially biphasic dose response; more exposure does not guarantee a larger response.
limits: General mechanisms, not direct equine hoof depth measurements, a wavelength superiority test or validation of a particular wrap.

authors: FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health
title: Compliance Guide for Laser Products
main_result: In its visible-spectrum example, Class IIIb spans 5-500 mW; classification also depends on wavelength and exposure duration.
limits: Historical guide with August 2008 address correction and a cover noting 2023 policy updates. Not a universal NIR threshold or LED classification.

authors: F. Dai; E. Dalla Costa; A. Giordano; E. U. L. Heinzl; P. Giongo; G. Pagnozzi; S. Cannas; G. Minozzi; M. Minero
title: Effects of BEMER physical vascular therapy in horses under training. A randomized, controlled double blind study
dose_or_settings: Two-week active and placebo blanket periods; 15 minutes of additional lunging daily; blood recovery assessed within one hour of exercise
main_result: The study did not confirm improved exercise recovery; apparent hematocrit and LF/HF differences favoring BEMER were not statistically significant.
limits: University record and full abstract read; journal full text not read. Not a hoof-injury trial or a comparison with LED.

authors: O. Brandenberger; A. Kalinovskiy; J. Korner; H. Genn; R. Burger; S. Leser
title: Effect of Bio-Electro-Magnetic-Energy-Regulation (BEMER) Horse Therapy on Cardiopulmonary Function and Recovery Quality After Isoflurane Anesthesia in 100 Horses Subjected to Pars-Plana Vitrectomy: An Investigator-Blinded Clinical Study
dose_or_settings: 15 minutes during isoflurane anesthesia for eye surgery; 1:1 allocation; recovery scale 10 best to 72 worst
main_result: Placebo recovery was significantly better: mean 16.1 (SD 7.15) versus BEMER 22.4 (SD 13.0); higher scores indicated worse recovery.
limits: Abstract and summary read, not full methods. Anesthesia recovery does not establish tendon rehabilitation outcomes. One author had a BEMER Int. AG affiliation.

authors: B. Carstanjen; M. Balali; Z. Gajewski; K. Furmanczyk; A. Bondzio; B. Remy; H. Hartmann
title: Short-term whole body vibration exercise in adult healthy horses
design: Before-after experiment in healthy adult horses; no separate sham group described
main_result: Cortisol and CK decreased (both P=.02); most other measurements did not change significantly. The short study reported no observed discomfort.
limits: Small healthy sample and brief follow-up; no long-term bone-strength, injury-prevention or clinical recovery outcome. No LED comparison.

authors: A. Edner; L.-G. Lindberg; H. Brostrom; A. Bergh
title: Does a magnetic blanket induce changes in muscular blood flow, skin temperature and muscular tension in horses?
dose_or_settings: 900 gauss; 60 minutes; crossover to the other condition on the following day
design: Prospective randomized blinded placebo-controlled crossover in healthy horses
main_result: Active and placebo blankets did not differ in muscle blood flow, skin temperature, mechanical pain threshold or behavior; both similarly increased skin temperature.
limits: Publisher summary read; first online April 30, 2014, journal year 2015. Back muscles, not lower-leg wraps. Static magnets are not PEMF.

title: Photomedicine in Veterinary Patients
main_result: General laser precautions address malignancy, retina, pregnant uterus, active bleeding and photosensitization; improper use can cause retinal injury or thermal burns.
limits: Reviewed September 2022; updated October 2025. No pregnancy study of lower-leg LED in mares or fixed post-injection waiting interval. Laser warnings are not measured LED thresholds.

authors: FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health
title: Frequently Asked Questions About Lasers
main_result: The hazard table distinguishes direct-beam eye hazards for Class IIIb from direct or reflected eye and skin hazards for Class IV.
limits: General laser safety; no equine LED eye-exposure limit, protective-eyewear specification or LED laser class.

title: myLEDmask 510(k) Summary, K223147
main_result: The device description states that a human facial LED mask includes shields intended to prevent LED light from reaching the eyes.
limits: Applicant description on PDF page 5; not an equine experiment or general FDA LED safety guidance. No horse eye threshold or particular equine-product authorization.

authors: A. D. Springborg; C. R. Wessel; L. P. K. Andersen; M. U. Werner
title: Methodology and applicability of the human contact burn injury model: A systematic review
species: humans; pigs in cited historical work
dose_or_settings: Historical cited example: 44 C for 6 hours; in the 44-51 C range each 1 C increase approximately halves time to equivalent injury
design: Systematic review; temperature-duration introduction paragraph read
main_result: The review reports microscopic epidermal cell death after 6 hours at 44 C in historical human/pig work; injury depends on temperature and duration.
limits: Secondary report of historical contact-heating experiments, not an equine LED test. No safe wrap temperature or session duration can be derived.

title: Learn to Recognize the Signs of Laminitis
main_result: Heat, increased digital pulse, weight shifting and characteristic lameness can signal laminitis; suspected laminitis requires an immediate veterinary call.
limits: Guidance, not a single-sign diagnosis or a light-treatment protocol. The linked PDF has no separate date.

title: Laminitis: Prevention & Treatment
journal_or_publisher: AAEP; PDF copy hosted by Association of Professional Farriers
main_result: Guidance describes case-specific veterinary management, soft footing and withholding grain and pasture pending advice; it does not recommend withholding all feed.
limits: Copy carries a 2020 copyright, not a verified article publication date. Professional procedures are not owner first-aid instructions; no LED evidence.

title: Scratches: a skin problem in horses
main_result: A hot, swollen, painful leg warrants veterinary contact; guidance describes gentle cleaning, dryness and cleaning reusable boots and wraps.
limits: Reviewed in 2021. No LED treatment evidence or permission to delay veterinary assessment.

title: Pastern Dermatitis (Scratches)
journal_or_publisher: UC Davis Center for Equine Health
main_result: Pastern dermatitis has multiple possible causes; guidance emphasizes early diagnosis and avoiding persistent moisture or prolonged moisture-trapping boots and wraps.
limits: No LED efficacy evidence or validated daily device exposure duration.

authors: Nelly Genoux; Christine Briant; Marianne Vidament; Lea Lansade; English translation: Karen Duffy
title: Habituation and sensitization
main_result: Guidance recommends small, gradual stimulus increases below the fear threshold, relaxation breaks and beginning in a quiet environment.
limits: General equine habituation guidance; no tested LED-wrap or massage-device sound, pressure, distance or duration protocol.

title: Proper bandaging technique and types of bandages in horse
main_result: Uneven, slipping or excessively tight bandages can cause pressure injury; guidance recommends clean, dry legs, smooth padding and even pressure.
limits: Traditional bandaging guidance, not an LED-wrap pressure measurement or fit chart. Padding and overlap instructions cannot automatically be transferred to electronic wraps.

title: Applying Leg Bandages
main_result: Guidance recommends even pressure and veterinary contact for new lameness, swelling above a bandage or suspected bandage bow.
limits: No individual author or publication year stated. Daily conventional-bandage changes are not an electronic-device wear-time instruction.

title: Electric Power Monthly, Table 5.6.A
main_result: The August 2026 US residential average electricity price is 18.16 cents/kWh, equivalent to $0.1816/kWh; the table labels 2026 data preliminary.
limits: Released October 23, 2026. Electricity unit price does not establish a device charging cost without measured energy use.

title: Biosecurity Guidelines
journal_or_publisher: AAEP; PDF copy hosted by California Department of Food and Agriculture
main_result: Guidance calls for removing organic material, cleaning before disinfection, respecting label contact times and fully drying shared reusable equipment.
limits: General biosecurity guidance does not establish that an electronic wrap can be immersed, machine-washed or exposed to a particular disinfectant.

title: Ringworm in Horses (Dermatophytosis)
journal_or_publisher: UC Davis Center for Equine Health
main_result: Dermatophytes can spread through direct contact and contaminated equipment; guidance recommends disinfecting contaminated items and assigning separate equipment to each horse.
limits: No electronic-wrap chemical compatibility, dilution or contact-time specification. Facility-floor advice is not a skin or device-cleaning instruction.

authors: Center for Food Security and Public Health, Iowa State University
title: Cleaning and Disinfection on the Farm: Grooming Equipment
main_result: Guidance describes removing visible debris, washing suitable equipment, disinfecting for the label contact time, rinsing and drying completely.
limits: Two-page tip sheet. Its bleach-volume examples depend on starting concentration and equipment suitability; they are not an electronic-wrap or skin-cleaning recipe.

authors: Shantel Julius / Julius Rehabilitation & Integrative Veterinary Services
title: Pricing Equine
tissue_or_site: Equine laser service; region not specified
main_result: The clinic lists equine laser treatment of 1-3 regions at $32 per application and a six-application package at $165.
limits: Hastings, Minnesota. Price effective date, wavelength, power and session duration not stated. Visit fees are separate; prices are not clinical efficacy evidence.

title: Services
main_result: The clinic lists regenerative laser therapy at $50 per session or $500-600 per protocol; the number of protocol sessions is not stated.
limits: Pilot Point, Texas. Different laser technology described as generating acoustic waves; not interchangeable with low-power laser or LED. No effective price date or efficacy evidence.

title: Pricing
main_result: The equine list states hock injections at $175 per hock and separately lists sedation at $71.
limits: Chatham, Virginia. Effective date and included drugs or joint count not stated. Another injection line has inconsistent anatomical wording; no total-care cost inferred.

title: Price List
tissue_or_site: Equine joint injections and farm calls
main_result: The January 1, 2025 list gives joint injections at $165-350, with details dependent on joint and medication; visit fees are separate.
limits: Laingsburg, Michigan. Not a 2026 effective price or an all-inclusive injection cost. Hock and fetlock are not priced separately.

title: SmartFlex product-family comparison table
main_result: The opened family table lists SmartFlex Pellets at $1.22/day and Senior Pellets at $1.27/day under SmartPaks daily pricing.
limits: Daily comparison-table prices, not verified monthly package or checkout prices. Dynamic individual-product price fields were unreadable; no clinical efficacy finding.

title: Simple Hoof Boot, Black, sold in pairs
main_result: Opened product text identifies a pair of hoof boots; the normal US list price was not available in the opened material.
limits: Product and category text were read. Search-snippet prices are excluded; no padded-pair cost or clinical efficacy established.

title: Cavallo Hoof Boot Cushion Pads, size 0-6
main_result: The opened page lists size 0-6 cushion-pad pairs at $29.95-39.95; the corresponding pad variant or thickness within that range is unclear.
limits: Separate pads, not a boot-inclusive price or proof of clinical benefit. No price effective date stated.

title: EasyCare Product Brochure, Cloud section
main_result: The opened historical brochure describes a closed-cell comfort pad included with Easyboot Cloud and states that the boot is not intended for riding.
limits: The current product offer was unreadable. Only the opened brochure supports this row; no current price, publication year or clinical efficacy is established.

title: Navicular Syndrome in Horses
tissue_or_site: Navicular bone, bursa, ligaments and deep digital flexor tendon
main_result: Navicular syndrome involves several structures; guidance describes diagnostic localization, imaging and long-term management including farriery changes where appropriate.
limits: Reference guidance, not a trial of light reaching or treating structures within the hoof.

title: Osteoarthritis of the Distal Tarsal Joints in Horses
main_result: Guidance describes diagnostic analgesia and radiography; radiographic change correlates poorly with lameness severity, and management is individualized.
limits: No proof that a lower-leg light wrap delivers an effective dose to hock joints or reverses osteoarthritis.

title: Disorders of the Pastern and Fetlock in Horses
main_result: The read high-ringbone section describes proximal interphalangeal osteoarthritis, imaging and case-dependent management; it does not establish LED-mediated cartilage or bone restoration.
limits: Reviewed July 2024; updated August 2025. Only high-ringbone section read; not a complete low-ringbone management review.

title: Tendinitis in Horses
tissue_or_site: Tendons; deep digital flexor tendon within hoof
main_result: Guidance describes ultrasound diagnosis, acute rest and cooling, and progressive controlled exercise; intratendinous corticosteroid injection is contraindicated.
limits: No universal healing timeline or weekly home exercise prescription; no evidence that an LED wrap shortens rehabilitation.

title: Suspensory Desmitis in Horses
main_result: For acute forelimb proximal suspensory desmitis, approximately 90% return to function is reported with rest and 3-6 months of controlled exercise.
limits: The figure is condition-specific, not an LED success rate; hindlimb, chronic and branch injuries have different prognoses and timelines.

title: Seasonal Change From Summer To Winter On Our Horses' Feet
main_result: Guidance advises preserving protective hoof material and considering boots or pads when needed; excessive lameness or refusal to move warrants professional assessment.
limits: No fixed duration for post-trim soreness or diagnosis excluding abscess and laminitis; light therapy was not tested.

title: Low quality of evidence for glucosamine-based nutraceuticals in equine joint disease: Review of in vivo studies
design: Review of 15 in vivo publications using predefined quality criteria
main_result: Only 3 of 15 publications exceeded the predefined 60% minimum quality threshold; generally low study quality limited meaningful interpretation.
limits: Publisher summary only. Journal year 2009; publisher first-online date January 5, 2010. Not evidence that all supplements are ineffective or a current comprehensive review.

authors: A. W. van Eps; J. A. Orsini
title: A comparison of seven methods for continuous therapeutic cooling of the equine digit
modality: Continuous therapeutic cooling; not light therapy
dose_or_settings: One forelimb cooled for 8 hours per period; at least 72 hours between periods; medians reported for hours 2-8
design: Crossover comparison of seven cooling methods
main_result: Median hoof-wall surface temperature was 5.2 C with an ice-water bag and 2.7 C with an ice-water boot; an ice boot that left the foot outside had a median of 25.7 C.
limits: Abstract only. Surface temperature, not lamellar temperature or clinical laminitis outcome. First online February 2, 2015; journal year 2016. No universal treatment duration.

title: Manual Therapy in Veterinary Patients
main_result: Guidance advises avoiding massage over infection, acute inflammation, tumors, recent surgical incisions or thrombosis; excessive pressure can damage tissues.
limits: Reviewed September 2022; updated March 2026. No equine massage-gun frequency, force, attachment or duration validated.

title: Evaluating the Benefits of Equine Massage Therapy: A Review of the Evidence and Current Practices
design: Narrative review; contraindication table and evidence sections read
main_result: The review describes preliminary manual-massage changes in heart rate and behavior; these observations do not establish injury healing or massage-gun efficacy.
limits: Historical narrative review, not a current systematic review. A cited 10-horse/pony preliminary study is not the review sample size. No validated percussion settings.

authors: Anna Bergh; Kjell Asplund; Irene Lund; Anna Bostrom; Heli Hyytiainen
title: A Systematic Review of Complementary and Alternative Veterinary Medicine in Sport and Companion Animals: Soft Tissue Mobilization
modality: Massage and stretching; not light therapy
design: Systematic review; 11 included studies: 9 massage and 2 stretching; 279 horses and 18 dogs across included studies
main_result: Eight studies had high and three moderate bias risk; evidence was insufficient to establish clinical efficacy or effectiveness of soft-tissue mobilization.
limits: 279 horses is the total across included studies, not a massage-gun trial. Short-term relaxation or range-of-motion changes do not establish injury prevention or tendon healing.

authors: Gillian Tabor; N. Nason; Christy Maddock
title: The effect percussive therapy on equine thoracic profile, mechanical nociceptive thresholds, spinal and limb kinematics and gait symmetry
tissue_or_site: Large superficial muscles; thoracic profile and gait
dose_or_settings: Theragun Pro 4th Generation; active and switched-off conditions, 12 minutes each, separated by 24 hours
design: Random-order blinded within-horse crossover in trained polo horses
main_result: Mechanical nociceptive threshold and stride length did not differ from sham; small thoracic-profile and spinal-motion changes included changes also seen with sham.
limits: University record and accepted manuscript abstract/methods read. Record gives early-online December 9, 2024, volume 21(1):71-79; issue year not verified. No lower-leg tendon or hoof percussion test or long-term safety finding.

authors: Ricardo Maia Ferreira; Rafael Silva; Pedro Vigario; Pedro Nunes Martins; Filipe Casanova; Ricardo Jorge Fernandes; Antonio Rodrigues Sampaio
title: The Effects of Massage Guns on Performance and Recovery: A Systematic Review
journal_or_publisher: Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology
modality: Percussive massage devices; not light therapy
design: Systematic review of 11 human studies; abstract, safety and limitations sections read
main_result: Ten included studies had moderate and one high bias risk; assessments were short term, and the review discussed safety concerns with aggressive or prolonged application.
limits: Human evidence does not validate equine device settings or anatomical restrictions. Discussed adverse events do not provide an incidence rate.

title: How to massage your horse
main_result: Practitioner advice recommends avoiding bony areas, joints and wounds, monitoring reactions, and seeking assessment for pain, spasm or unexplained lameness.
limits: Manual-massage advice from a qualified practitioner hosted by an insurer; not a controlled efficacy or device-setting study. Promotional benefit claims are not carried into this register.
